mainTopic: Drawing water on שבת: balconies over water (כוף וגוד and balcony sizes) and water channels passing through courtyards and between windows
overview: This amud opens with the end of a ברייתא. In it, רבי חנניא בן עקביא allows cutting a 4x4 טפחים hole in a large balcony over the water and drawing water through it. אביי rejects the attempt to link this to רבי יהודה: רבי יהודה may accept only גוד אחית, not כוף וגוד, and רבי חנניא בן עקביא may mean only the ים של טבריה. אביי and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע then work out smaller balcony sizes for a balcony near a wall, one with upright partitions, and one in a corner. The full 4x4 אמות size is needed only for a free-standing balcony shaped like a mortar. A new משנה follows. It rules that a water channel passing through a courtyard needs partitions at both ends, while רבי יהודה says the courtyard wall above it is enough, and the חכמים reject his proof from the channel of אבל. Another ברייתא about a channel between windows leads the גמרא to explain that the 3 or 4 טפחים measure the channel's banks, so the ruling does not clash with רבי יוחנן's rules about a כרמלית and a מקום פטור. The answer about Torah-level domains continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: Cut a Four-by-Four Hole and Draw Water
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of רבי חנניא בן עקביא's ברייתא: in a large balcony, one cuts a 4x4 טפחים hole and draws water through it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He carves a hole in it, four by four handbreadths, and draws water.
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing a ברייתא that started on the previous amud. רבי חנניא בן עקביא rules that a person cuts a 4x4 טפחים hole in a big balcony over the water and may draw water through it on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are no real walls around the hole. The idea is that the balcony floor around the hole is pictured as bending down and becoming walls 10 טפחים high on all sides (כוף וגוד). That makes the space under the hole count as an enclosed area, so drawing water through it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: carves / cuts out a hole
four by four (טפחים), the minimum size of a halachic space
draws (fills up) water
a balcony jutting out over the water (the subject of the case)

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody actually builds walls here. The 'walls' are imaginary: the floor around the hole is treated as if it were bent downward.

phrases.english: he carves in it [a hole of] four by four [handbreadths]
phrases.notes: 'In it' means in the balcony, which is 4x4 אמות.

phrases.english: and draws water.
phrases.notes: Allowed because the surrounding floor is viewed as bent down into walls.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹקֵק בָּהּ אַרְבַּע עַל אַרְבַּע וּמְמַלֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא, begun on the previous amud, that is being cited to compare רבי חנניא בן עקביא with רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a 4x4 אמות balcony over water, one may cut a 4x4 טפחים hole and draw water through it, using the principle of כוף וגוד.

steps.title: אביי: רבי יהודה Only Accepts Extending a Wall Downward
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the claim that רבי יהודה agrees with רבי חנניא בן עקביא. רבי יהודה may accept only גוד אחית מחיצתא, not כוף וגוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But maybe that is not so. רבי יהודה only said his ruling there because he holds 'extend the partition downward.' But 'bend and extend'? No.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the earlier speaker, who said these two תנאים hold the same idea. He shows that רבי יהודה's view may be much narrower.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גוד אחית takes a wall that really exists and imagines it continuing straight down. כוף וגוד is a bigger step: it takes a flat, horizontal floor, imagines it bending into a wall, and then stretches that wall down. A person can accept the first and reject the second, so רבי יהודה is no proof for רבי חנניא בן עקביא.

keyTerms.meaning: but perhaps it is not so (a formula for rejecting a proof)
he only said [his ruling] up to this point (limits a view to its case)
extend and lower the partition: an existing wall is viewed as reaching down
bend and extend: a horizontal surface is viewed as bending down into a wall

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up these two ideas. גוד אחית starts from a wall that already exists. כוף וגוד first has to turn a flat floor into a wall.
steps.whyThisMatters: This distinction between גוד אחית and כוף וגוד comes back throughout הלכות מחיצות in Eruvin.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: Responding to the earlier speaker (רבה), who linked the two views.

phrases.english: But perhaps that is not so,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda only stated his opinion there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of the courtyard wall passing over the cistern.

phrases.english: because he says: 'extend and lower the partition,'
but 'bend and extend'? No.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְדִילְמָא לָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the attempt to equate רבי יהודה's position with the ברייתא of רבי חנניא בן עקביא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רבי יהודה supports רבי חנניא בן עקביא's method.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison ignores the real difference between גוד אחית, which extends an existing wall, and כוף וגוד, which turns a horizontal surface into a wall.

steps.title: אביי: רבי חנניא בן עקביא May Only Mean the ים של טבריה
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds a second difference. רבי חנניא בן עקביא may have been lenient only for the ים של טבריה, which has clear banks and is surrounded by towns and enclosures, but not for other waters.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חנניא בן עקביא only said his ruling there about the ים של טבריה, since it has banks and towns and enclosures surround it. But with other waters? No.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues his rejection from the other side. Even רבי חנניא בן עקביא's leniency may be limited to one special body of water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ים של טבריה is ringed by banks, towns and fenced areas, so it already looks somewhat enclosed. That may be why a small fix, the imagined כוף וגוד, was enough there. So רבי חנניא בן עקביא's rule may not be a general principle, which weakens the comparison even more.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sea of Tiberias (כנרת)
banks / rims around a body of water
fenced enclosures (outside town)
other bodies of water

steps.whatToRemember: אביי says the two views may not match at all. רבי יהודה may hold only גוד אחית, not כוף וגוד. רבי חנניא בן עקביא may apply כוף וגוד only to the ים של טבריה, because its borders make it look enclosed.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא הָתָם,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chananya ben Akavya only stated his opinion there,
with regard to the Sea of Tiberias,
since it has banks,
and towns and enclosures surround it,
but with regard to other waters, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of אביי's rejection. Step 2 limited רבי יהודה; this step limits רבי חנניא בן עקביא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits רבי חנניא בן עקביא's leniency to the ים של טבריה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison assumes רבי חנניא בן עקביא stated a general rule, but his leniency may depend on the special surroundings of the ים של טבריה.

steps.title: אביי: Balcony Size Needed When It Is Near a Wall
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that, according to רבי חנניא בן עקביא, a balcony within 3 טפחים of a wall needs to be only 4 אמות long and a little over 11 טפחים wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: According to רבי חנניא בן עקביא, if the balcony was less than three טפחים from the wall, its length must be four אמות, and its width eleven טפחים and a bit.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts a new point. He works out the smallest balcony that still works under רבי חנניא בן עקביא's method when the balcony sits close to a wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gap of less than 3 טפחים counts as closed (לבוד), so the hole can borrow those 3 טפחים and needs only a little over 1 טפח of its own, making 4x4. Length: 4 אמות is 24 טפחים, which leaves 10 טפחים on each side of the 4-wide hole to 'bend down' into two walls. Width: a bit over 1 טפח for the hole plus 10 טפחים to bend into the fourth wall gives 11 and a bit, and the real wall is the third side.

keyTerms.meaning: close to the wall
less than three handbreadths (a gap this small counts as closed: לָבוּד)
cubits (one אמה = 6 טפחים)
and any small amount more

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix units: the length is in אמות (4 אמות = 24 טפחים), but the width is in טפחים (11 and a bit).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how לבוד and כוף וגוד can work together to cut down the required size of the balcony.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
And according to the statement of Rabbi Chananya ben Akavya,
if the balcony was near the wall
by less than three handbreadths,
phrases.notes: The gap counts as closed (לבוד), so it joins the hole.

phrases.english: its length must be four cubits,
phrases.notes: 24 טפחים = 10 + 4 (hole) + 10.

phrases.english: and its width eleven [handbreadths] and a bit.
phrases.notes: A bit over 1 טפח for the hole, plus 10 to bend down as the fourth wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: וּלְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the comparison is rejected, אביי turns to apply רבי חנניא בן עקביא's method to a new case: a balcony near a wall.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רבי חנניא בן עקביא, a balcony within 3 טפחים of a wall needs a length of 4 אמות and a width of a little more than 11 טפחים.

steps.title: A balcony with upright partitions needs only six טפחים and a bit
steps.stepSummary: Continuing אביי's measurements: if the balcony has upright partitions, they must be 10 טפחים tall, and the balcony must be 6 טפחים plus two tiny amounts wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the balcony was upright, its height must be ten טפחים, and its width six טפחים and two tiny amounts.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives another, smaller size for a balcony under רבי חנניא בן עקביא's ruling. This size is for a balcony that has upright partitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the balcony already has real partitions 10 טפחים tall, it does not need a large floor area. It only needs room for the 4x4 hole plus a little more than a טפח on each side to stand on. That gives 6 טפחים and two tiny extra amounts.

keyTerms.meaning: Upright; here, a balcony with upright partitions around it
Its height is ten טפחים, the standard height of a valid partition
A tiny, minimal amount

phrases.english: If it was upright,
phrases.notes: According to רבינו חננאל, this means it had upright partitions on all sides.

phrases.english: its height must be ten handbreadths,
and its width six handbreadths and two minimal amounts.
phrases.notes: This is the 4-טפח hole plus slightly more than one טפח on each side.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה זְקוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's list of minimum balcony sizes from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A balcony with upright partitions needs walls 10 טפחים tall and a width of only 6 טפחים plus two tiny amounts.

steps.title: A balcony in a corner needs only two טפחים and a bit
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says that a balcony sitting in the corner between two walls needs partitions 10 טפחים tall and a width of only 2 טפחים plus two tiny amounts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, said: If it stood in a corner, its height must be ten טפחים, and its width two טפחים and two tiny amounts.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא adds an even smaller size. This size is for a balcony placed in a corner between two walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a corner, the two existing walls of the building already serve as real partitions. Because of that, the balcony itself needs much less of its own space, so the required width drops to just 2 טפחים plus two tiny amounts.

keyTerms.meaning: A corner, where two walls meet
Son of

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
If it was standing in a corner,
its height must be ten handbreadths,
and its width two handbreadths and two minimal amounts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another, even smaller case to the list of balcony sizes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A balcony in a corner needs partitions 10 טפחים tall and a width of only 2 טפחים plus two tiny amounts.

steps.title: When is the full four-by-four אמות balcony ever needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if all these smaller balconies are valid, in what case does the ברייתא's size of 4 אמות by 4 אמות apply?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, regarding what was taught that רבי חנניא בן עקביא says, 'A balcony that has four אמות by four אמות: one carves a four-by-four hole in it and draws water', how can such a case be found?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back רבי חנניא בן עקביא's own words. It asks when his larger size would ever be needed, given all the smaller sizes just listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא named 4 אמות by 4 אמות as the size of the balcony. But steps 4 through 6 showed that much smaller balconies also work. So the גמרא wants a real case where the full size is truly needed, otherwise the ברייתא's number seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: But then; introduces a difficulty that follows from what was just said
That which was taught in a ברייתא
Carves or cuts out
How can you find it? (In what case does this apply?)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not questioning whether the ברייתא is correct. It is only asking which case the ברייתא's specific measurement fits.

phrases.english: But then, that which is taught in a baraita,
Rabbi Ḥananya ben Akavya says:

phrases.aramaic: גְּזוּזְטְרָא שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת עַל אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת —
phrases.english: A balcony that has four cubits by four cubits,

phrases.aramaic: חוֹקֵק בָּהּ אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה וּמְמַלֵּא,
phrases.english: one carves in it four by four handbreadths and draws water,
how can you find such a case?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the smaller sizes from steps 4 through 6 to ask what case the ברייתא's larger size refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case actually requires a balcony of 4 אמות by 4 אמות?
steps.kashyaTarget: The measurement stated in רבי חנניא בן עקביא's ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If smaller balconies are enough, the ברייתא's stated size seems to have no case that needs it.

steps.title: A free-standing balcony shaped like a mortar
steps.stepSummary: The full 4x4 אמות size is needed for a balcony built like a mortar, standing on its own pillars away from any wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where it is made like a mortar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The ברייתא is talking about a free-standing balcony that gets no help from any wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mortar-shaped balcony stands alone over the water on its own supports, with no building walls nearby. All of its partitions must be built out of its own floor space. That is why it needs the full 4 אמות by 4 אמות, unlike the smaller balconies that lean on nearby walls or corners.

keyTerms.meaning: Made or built
A mortar; here, a free-standing balcony on its own pillars

steps.whatToRemember: All the smaller sizes rely on outside help, such as nearby walls, a corner, or upright partitions. רבי חנניא בן עקביא's full 4x4 אמות size is for a balcony that stands completely alone, like a mortar.

phrases.english: Where it is made like a mortar.
phrases.notes: It stands on its own pillars over the water, far from any wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּעֲבִידָא כִּי אֲסִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by identifying the case the ברייתא refers to.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A free-standing, mortar-shaped balcony with no help from any wall, so all of its partitions come from its own floor area.

steps.title: A water channel in a courtyard needs partitions at both ends
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that you may not draw water on שבת from a channel passing through a courtyard unless partitions 10 טפחים high stand at its entrance and its exit.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A water channel that passes through a courtyard: you may not draw water from it on שבת, unless they made a partition for it ten טפחים high at the place where it enters and at the place where it exits.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a rule. You may not draw water on שבת from a channel flowing through a courtyard unless partitions stand where it comes in and where it goes out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The channel comes from outside and leaves again, so it counts as its own separate area, not part of the courtyard. Lifting water out of it into the courtyard would be carrying between two areas. Partitions at both ends close the channel in and make it part of the courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: a water channel or small stream
draw (fill up) water
a partition
handbreadths (10 טפחים is the standard height of a partition)
the entrance and the exit (where the channel enters and leaves the courtyard)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'אמה' means a water channel, not the measurement 'אמה' (cubit) from the balcony discussion just before.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ אַמַּת הַמַּיִם שֶׁהִיא עוֹבֶרֶת בֶּחָצֵר
phrases.english: MISHNA: A water channel that passes through a courtyard
one may not draw water from it on Shabbat

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עָשׂוּ לָהּ מְחִיצָה
phrases.english: unless they made a partition for it
ten handbreadths high
at the entrance and at the exit

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּת הַמַּיִם שֶׁהִיא עוֹבֶרֶת בֶּחָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה on a new topic, moving from balconies over water to water channels inside courtyards.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drawing water from a courtyard channel on שבת requires 10-טפח partitions at both the entrance and the exit.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says the courtyard wall counts as a partition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees: the courtyard wall that runs over the channel already counts as a partition, so nothing new needs to be built.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the wall that is on top of it is judged as a partition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues with the first opinion. He says the courtyard wall passing over the channel is already good enough as a partition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courtyard wall is built over the channel, so it hangs above the water. רבי יהודה treats that wall as if it extends down into the channel and closes it off. Because of this, there is no need to build special partitions in the water.

keyTerms.meaning: a wall (here, the courtyard wall)
on top of it (over the channel)
is judged as / is treated as
'stretch down the partition': we view a hanging wall as if it reached down

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹתֶל שֶׁעַל גַּבָּהּ תִּידּוֹן מִשּׁוּם מְחִיצָה
phrases.english: the wall that is on top of it is considered as a partition

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting opinion to the תנא קמא in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The courtyard wall over the channel counts as a partition, so no extra partition is needed.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's proof from the channel of אבל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה supports his view with a story: in אבל, people drew water from a channel on שבת with the approval of the זקנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: There was a story with the channel of אבל, from which people would draw water on שבת by the ruling of the זקנים!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה brings a real-life story to prove his opinion. The זקנים let people draw water from the channel in אבל on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Presumably the channel in אבל had no special partitions, only the courtyard walls passing over it. If the זקנים still allowed drawing water, that shows the wall above counts as a partition, just as רבי יהודה says.

keyTerms.meaning: an incident or story (brought as a proof)
the name of a town
by the authority of the Elders (the sages)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said
there was an incident with the channel of Avel
from which they would draw water
by the authority of the Elders on Shabbat!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story as support for רבי יהודה's ruling in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that the wall above the channel counts as a partition
steps.raayaSupportSource: The זקנים allowed drawing water on שבת from the channel in אבל

steps.title: The חכמים reject the proof: that channel was too small
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that the channel in אבל was below the minimum size, so it never needed a partition in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: That was because it did not have the required size.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יהודה's story. They say it proves nothing, because that channel was too small to count as a separate area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a channel deep and wide enough counts as its own separate area. The channel in אבל was smaller than that, so drawing from it was allowed even with no partition. The story therefore does not show that a wall above works as a partition.

keyTerms.meaning: they (the other חכמים) said to him
the required size (minimum measurement)
an in-between area, neither fully private nor fully public, from which carrying is forbidden by the חכמים

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's dispute: the תנא קמא requires real partitions at both ends of the channel, while רבי יהודה says the wall above is enough. The חכמים say the אבל story only worked because that channel was too small to matter.

phrases.english: They said to him
because it did not have the required size.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בָּהּ כַּשִּׁיעוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof, not רבי יהודה's opinion itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story involved a channel too small to need a partition, so it cannot teach anything about a wall above counting as a partition.

steps.title: A ברייתא: a partition on only one side is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: a partition at only the entrance, or only the exit, is not enough. Both ends need a 10-טפח partition.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The חכמים taught: If they made a partition at the entrance but not at the exit, or at the exit but not at the entrance, you may not draw water from it on שבת, unless they made a partition of ten טפחים at both the exit and the entrance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that spells out the תנא קמא's rule more clearly. Fixing only one side of the channel does not help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'entrance and exit,' and the ברייתא makes sure we understand this means both are needed. If even one side stays open, the channel is still connected to the outside and is not part of the courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: the חכמים taught (opens a ברייתא)
a teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught
if they made a partition for it at the entrance
but did not make one for it at the exit
or they made one for it at the exit
but did not make one for it at the entrance
one may not draw water from it on Shabbat

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עָשׂוּ לָהּ מְחִיצָה
phrases.english: unless they made a partition for it
of ten handbreadths at the exit and at the entrance.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן עָשׂוּ לָהּ בִּכְנִיסָה וְלֹא עָשׂוּ לָהּ בִּיצִיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that restates and clarifies the תנא קמא of the משנה (step 9).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A partition on only one side does not permit drawing water. Both entrance and exit need 10-טפח partitions.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's view repeated in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא repeats רבי יהודה's view that the courtyard wall above the channel counts as a partition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the wall that is on top of it is judged as a partition.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא repeats רבי יהודה's disagreement in the same words as the משנה. It is setting up his story, which comes next with an added detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבי יהודה's view, even the one-sided case in the ברייתא would be fine. The wall above already closes off both ends, so no new partitions are needed anywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: the first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
a dispute between opinions
a hanging partition (a wall that does not reach the ground or water)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹתֶל שֶׁעַל גַּבָּהּ תִּידּוֹן מִשּׁוּם מְחִיצָה.
phrases.english: the wall that is on top of it is considered as a partition.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר כּוֹתֶל שֶׁעַל גַּבָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא's version of רבי יהודה's dissent, which disagrees with step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wall above the channel counts as a partition.

steps.title: The ברייתא's story: the channel from אבל to צפורי
steps.stepSummary: In the ברייתא, רבי יהודה tells the story in more detail: the channel ran from אבל to צפורי, and people drew from it on שבת with the approval of the זקנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: There was a story with a water channel that ran from אבל to צפורי, and people would draw water from it on שבת by the ruling of the זקנים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה repeats his proof, and the ברייתא adds that the channel ran from אבל all the way to צפורי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives רבי יהודה's proof in a fuller form: it names the channel's route, from אבל to צפורי. The claim is the same as in the משנה. The זקנים allowed drawing water with only the courtyard wall above the channel, so that wall must count as a partition. The next step gives the חכמים' reply as it appears in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Tzippori, a major town in the גליל
that was coming (flowing) from
'an action is great': a real-life ruling is strong proof

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא confirms that both ends of the channel need partitions according to the תנא קמא, while רבי יהודה relies on the wall above. His story is now about a long channel from אבל to צפורי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said
there was an incident with the water channel
that went from Avel to Tzippori
and they would draw water from it on Shabbat
by the authority of the Elders.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאַמַּת הַמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יהודה's view in step 14 with the ברייתא's fuller version of the story from step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that the wall above counts as a partition
steps.raayaSupportSource: The זקנים allowed drawing water on שבת from the channel running from אבל to צפורי

steps.title: The חכמים reject the proof from the channel of אבל
steps.stepSummary: In the ברייתא, the חכמים answer רבי יהודה that the channel in אבל was not ten טפחים deep or not four טפחים wide, so it proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: You want to bring a proof from there?! That was only because the channel was not ten טפחים deep, or not four טפחים wide.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יהודה's story from the ברייתא version. The channel in אבל was too small to count as its own area, so drawing from it was always allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה used the story to show that a courtyard wall above the channel works as a partition. The חכמים say the story shows nothing about partitions. A channel that is less than ten deep or less than four wide is not a separate domain at all, so it never needed any partition.

keyTerms.meaning: "From there you bring a proof?!" A standard way to reject a proof.
Deep
Its width
Handbreadths, a unit of measurement

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a repeat of step 12 by mistake. Step 12 was the חכמים' answer in the משנה. This is their answer as it appears in the fuller ברייתא, which the גמרא itself quotes.

phrases.english: They said to him: From there you bring a proof?!

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה עֲמוּקָּה עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים
phrases.english: That was because it was not ten handbreadths deep
or not four handbreadths wide.
phrases.notes: If it fails either measurement, it is not a separate domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מִשָּׁם רְאָיָיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof רבי יהודה brought in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely, without rejecting the story itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The channel in אבל was below the minimum size of a domain (ten deep and four wide), so it never needed a partition.

steps.title: Another teaching about a water channel between windows
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: if a channel runs between two windows, the תנא קמא allows drawing water if it is less than three טפחים and forbids it at three. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל sets the limit at four.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in another ברייתא: A water channel that passes between the windows of two houses. If it is less than three טפחים, a person may lower a bucket and draw water. If it is three, he may not. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: If it is less than four, he may lower a bucket and draw. If it is four, he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with a disagreement over the size at which you may no longer draw water from a channel through a window.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a channel running between houses, with people lowering buckets into it from their windows. The תנא קמא says three טפחים makes it forbidden, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says only four does. The ברייתא does not say what is being measured, which sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: "It was taught in another ברייתא"
Windows
Lowers a bucket
Fills, meaning draws water
A תנא who disagrees with the first opinion

phrases.english: It was taught in another baraita:
A water channel that passes between the windows,
if it is less than three handbreadths,
one may lower a bucket and draw water.
If it is three, one may not lower a bucket and draw water.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
If it is less than four, one may lower a bucket and draw water;
if it is four, one may not lower a bucket and draw water.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא on a related case of drawing water from a channel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: drawing is allowed if the channel is under three טפחים and forbidden at three. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: allowed under four and forbidden at four.

steps.title: What do the three and four handbreadths measure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא is measuring and suggests the width of the channel itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If you say the measurement is of the water channel itself...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the numbers three and four describe. It offers a first guess: the width of the channel. This is a setup line that leads straight into the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave numbers without saying what they measure. Before the גמרא can understand the dispute, it needs to know this. The first guess is that the channel itself is three or four טפחים wide.

keyTerms.meaning: "What case are we dealing with?"
"If you say," which introduces a possible answer
Itself

phrases.english: With what are we dealing?
If you say: with the water channel itself,
phrases.notes: That is, the channel is three or four handbreadths wide.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the measurements in the ברייתא from step 17 refer to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the three or four טפחים measure the channel's own width or something else.

steps.title: Does this make רב דימי's rule a dispute among תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: If the numbers measure the channel, then רב דימי's rule in the name of רבי יוחנן, that a כרמלית is never less than four טפחים, would become a disagreement between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what about the teaching that when רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A כרמלית cannot be less than four טפחים? Shall we say he stated his teaching according to only one side of a dispute between תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first guess. If the channel's width is what matters, the two תנאים are really arguing about the smallest size of a כרמלית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drawing water from the channel into a house means carrying from a כרמלית into a רשות היחיד. The water channel counts as a כרמלית, which is why drawing becomes forbidden at all. So if the תנא קמא forbids drawing at three wide, he holds that a three-wide area is already a כרמלית. That clashes with רבי יוחנן's rule of four, which would then match only רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and lose its status as an undisputed rule.

keyTerms.meaning: "When רב דימי came," meaning from ארץ ישראל to בבל
A rabbinic in-between domain, neither public nor private
"Shall we say it is a dispute between תנאים?"
His teaching

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא prefers not to make a well-known אמורא rule depend on one side of a תנאים dispute. That pressure forces it to rethink what the ברייתא is measuring.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי
phrases.english: But then, that which was said when Rav Dimi came
in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
A karmelit cannot be less than four handbreadths wide.
Shall we say he stated his teaching according to one side of a dispute between tanna'im?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggestion from step 18 that the measurement is the channel's own width.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the ברייתא's three and four טפחים refer to the width of the channel itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading, the תנא קמא treats a three-wide channel as a כרמלית. That contradicts רבי יוחנן's rule that a כרמלית is at least four, and turns his rule into one side of a תנאים dispute.

steps.title: The numbers measure the channel's banks, and the case is about passing the bucket
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the קשיא from רב דימי's rule about a כרמלית. The three or four טפחים do not measure the channel. They measure its banks, and the ברייתא is about moving the bucket across them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the measurement is of its banks, and the case is about passing objects across.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the idea that the ברייתא measures the channel itself. It says the numbers measure the banks of the channel, and the case is about passing the bucket across them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the numbers measured the channel, the תנאים would be arguing about the minimum size of a כרמלית, and that would clash with רב דימי. Now the argument is about the banks. A bank smaller than the limit counts as a מקום פטור, so the bucket may pass from the window (רשות היחיד) over the bank to the channel (כרמלית) and come back full. At three or four טפחים the bank becomes a real domain, and passing across it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. The גמרא is dropping the previous explanation.
Its banks or sides, meaning the edges of the channel.
To exchange or pass across, moving an object from one domain to another by way of a third area.
An exempt area, too small to count as any domain for שבת.

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא's numbers are no longer about the size of the channel (the כרמלית). They are now about the banks. The channel stays a כרמלית no matter what.
steps.whyThisMatters: This new reading is what lets the ברייתא stand without clashing with רבי יוחנן's rule that a כרמלית is never smaller than four טפחים.

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to its banks,
phrases.notes: The three or four טפחים measure the banks of the channel, not the channel itself.

phrases.english: and it is about exchanging (passing across).
phrases.notes: The bucket is moved from the window, over the bank, to the water and back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בַּאֲגַפֶּיהָ, וּלְהַחְלִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19 by giving the ברייתא a new subject: the banks, not the channel.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case: the ברייתא is moved from measuring the כרמלית to measuring a מקום פטור.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The numbers measure the channel's width, so the תנאים argue about the minimum size of a כרמלית.
steps.terutzMaskana: The numbers measure the banks, which serve as a מקום פטור for passing the bucket, so רב דימי's rule about a כרמלית is not contradicted.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי יוחנן forbids exchanging objects through a small exempt area
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that an area smaller than four by four may be used by people of both domains to adjust their loads, but they may not exchange objects through it. That seems to forbid exactly what the new answer allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a place that is not four by four טפחים may be used by people of the private domain and the public domain to adjust loads on their shoulders, as long as they do not exchange objects through it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It quotes רבי יוחנן's rule that passing objects through a small exempt area is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 allowed the bucket to pass from the window over a small bank (a מקום פטור) to the channel. רבי יוחנן says that people may rest their loads on a מקום פטור, but they may not use it to hand objects from one domain to the other. So how can the ברייתא allow passing the bucket?

keyTerms.meaning: But look! A standard way of opening a challenge.
When he came, meaning when the sage arrived in Babylonia from ארץ ישראל.
To shoulder, meaning to rest or adjust a load on one's shoulder.
Provided that they do not exchange objects through it.

phrases.english: But when Rav Dimi came (from the Land of Israel),
phrases.notes: This opens the challenge.

phrases.english: he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
phrases.notes: The attribution of the rule being quoted.

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה —
phrases.english: A place that does not have four by four (handbreadths),
phrases.notes: Such a place is a מקום פטור.

phrases.english: it is permitted for the people of the private domain
and for the people of the public domain
to adjust loads on their shoulders on it,
phrases.notes: Each side may rest its burden there.

phrases.english: provided that they do not exchange (objects through it).
phrases.notes: This is the point that clashes with step 20.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 20, which allowed exchanging through a מקום פטור.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 20 that the bucket may be passed across the banks, which act as a מקום פטור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן explicitly forbids exchanging objects between two domains by way of a מקום פטור, so the ברייתא should not allow it.

steps.title: Beginning of the answer: רב דימי was talking about Torah-level domains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer the challenge. רבי יוחנן's ban on exchanging applies where both domains are Torah-level domains.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the case involves domains that exist by Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering the challenge by pointing out what רבי יוחנן's case was about. This is a setup line: it describes "there," and the contrast with "here" in our ברייתא is coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יוחנן's case, the two domains are a real רשות היחיד and a real רשות הרבים, which are domains under Torah law. The חכמים forbade exchanging through the מקום פטור there, so that people would not end up carrying straight from one Torah domain into the other. The answer is pointing toward a difference: in our ברייתא the channel is only a כרמלית, which is a rabbinic category.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in the other case being compared.
Domains defined by Torah law: a true רשות היחיד and a true רשות הרבים.
An in-between area that the חכמים treat as a domain; it is not a domain under Torah law.

steps.confusionAlert: This line finishes only the "there" half of the answer. The "here" half, about our channel being a כרמלית, comes in the text right on the next amud.

phrases.english: There, (it involves) domains by Torah law,
phrases.notes: This sets up the contrast with our case, which involves a rabbinic כרמלית.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם רְשׁוּיוֹת דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the קשיא of step 21 by limiting רבי יוחנן's rule to Torah-level domains.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: Torah-level domains versus a rabbinic כרמלית.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's ban on exchanging through a מקום פטור applies everywhere, including our ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban was said about Torah-level domains, where there is a worry that people will carry directly from one to the other. Our case is different, as the next line will explain.
